claims.title: The Dacian kingdom
claims.summary: The Dacians built a powerful kingdom in the Carpathian arc, fortified by stone strongholds in the Orastie Mountains with their capital at Sarmizegetusa Regia, the nucleus of Dacian power.

sources.label: Dacian Fortresses of the Orastie Mountains

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-82bce-the-dacian-kingdom, claim TL:ROU:event:82bce:the-dacian-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Trajan's first Dacian war
claims.summary: The emperor Trajan invaded Dacia and forced King Decebalus to terms, installing a Roman garrison in the Dacian capital at Sarmizegetusa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-101-trajan-s-first-dacian-war, claim TL:ROU:event:101:trajan-s-first-dacian-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of Dacia and the Roman province
claims.summary: In a second war Trajan subdued the whole country; Decebalus killed himself, and Dacia became a Roman province whose colonists made Latin its language, the root of Romanian.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-106-conquest-of-dacia-and-the-roman-province, claim TL:ROU:event:106:conquest-of-dacia-and-the-roman-province, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Trajan's Column commemorates the conquest
claims.summary: The Dacian wars were commemorated in Rome on Trajan's Column, a 38-metre marble monument whose spiral frieze of more than 2,600 figures narrates the two campaigns against the Dacians.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-113-trajan-s-column-commemorates-the-conquest, claim TL:ROU:event:113:trajan-s-column-commemorates-the-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Aurelian abandons Dacia
claims.summary: Under mounting frontier pressure the emperor Aurelian withdrew the Roman army and administration from Dacia, yet a Latin-speaking population persisted, carrying forward the Daco-Roman heritage.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-271-aurelian-abandons-dacia, claim TL:ROU:event:271:aurelian-abandons-dacia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Basarab I founds Wallachia
claims.summary: The voivode Basarab I defeated King Charles I of Hungary at Posada, winning recognition of Wallachia's autonomy and establishing the first Romanian principality.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1330-basarab-i-founds-wallachia, claim TL:ROU:event:1330:basarab-i-founds-wallachia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bogdan I founds Moldavia
claims.summary: The Vlach voivode Bogdan I crossed the Carpathians from Maramures and wrenched Moldavia from Hungarian vassalage, founding the second Romanian principality.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1359-bogdan-i-founds-moldavia, claim TL:ROU:event:1359:bogdan-i-founds-moldavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Stephen the Great's victory at Vaslui
claims.summary: Stephen the Great of Moldavia crushed a much larger Ottoman army at Vaslui, one of his celebrated victories in a long resistance to the Turks that won him renown across Christian Europe.

sources.label: Stephen, prince of Moldavia (Stephen the Great)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1475-stephen-the-great-s-victory-at-vaslui, claim TL:ROU:event:1475:stephen-the-great-s-victory-at-vaslui, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vlad III the Impaler resists the Ottomans
claims.summary: Vlad III of Wallachia, remembered for impaling his enemies, fought a savage campaign against Ottoman power; his reputation later inspired the literary figure of Dracula.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1462-vlad-iii-the-impaler-resists-the-ottomans, claim TL:ROU:event:1462:vlad-iii-the-impaler-resists-the-ottomans, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Phanariot regime
claims.summary: Under Ottoman suzerainty the Porte appointed the princes of Wallachia and Moldavia from among the Greek Phanariot families of Constantinople, a period of heavy tribute and misrule that lasted until 1821.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1711-the-phanariot-regime, claim TL:ROU:event:1711:the-phanariot-regime, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Horezu Monastery and Brancovan art
claims.summary: Prince Constantin Brancoveanu founded the monastery of Horezu in Wallachia, a masterpiece of the 'Brancovan' style whose school of mural and icon painting influenced religious art across the Balkans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1690-horezu-monastery-and-brancovan-art, claim TL:ROU:event:1690:horezu-monastery-and-brancovan-art, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of the Principalities
claims.summary: Moldavia (5 January) and Wallachia (24 January) elected Alexandru Ioan Cuza as their common prince, uniting the two principalities and founding the modern Romanian state.

sources.label: 24 January 1859: A Glimpse on the Union of Romanian Principalities

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1859-union-of-the-principalities, claim TL:ROU:event:1859:union-of-the-principalities, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cuza's reforms
claims.summary: Prince Cuza carried through agrarian reform giving land to some 400,000 peasant families, reformed law and taxation, introduced the metric system and a French-modelled civil code.

sources.label: 24 January 1859: A Glimpse on the Union of Romanian Principalities

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1864-cuza-s-reforms, claim TL:ROU:event:1864:cuza-s-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence recognised at the Congress of Berlin
claims.summary: After fighting in the Russo-Turkish War, Romania's full independence was recognised by the great powers at the Congress of Berlin in 1878, though it ceded southern Bessarabia to Russia.

sources.label: 24 January 1859: A Glimpse on the Union of Romanian Principalities

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1878-independence-recognised-at-the-congress-of, claim TL:ROU:event:1878:independence-recognised-at-the-congress-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kingdom of Romania proclaimed
claims.summary: Romania was proclaimed a kingdom and Carol I, prince since 1866, became its first king, completing the country's emergence as a sovereign European state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1881-kingdom-of-romania-proclaimed, claim TL:ROU:event:1881:kingdom-of-romania-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Romania enters the First World War
claims.summary: Romania joined the Allies in 1916 seeking the Romanian lands of Austria-Hungary, especially Transylvania; despite early defeats, the collapse of the empires opened the way to union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1916-romania-enters-the-first-world-war, claim TL:ROU:event:1916:romania-enters-the-first-world-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Transylvania with Romania
claims.summary: A great national assembly of Romanians at Alba Iulia proclaimed the union of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania, the central act in the creation of Greater Romania.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1918-union-of-transylvania-with-romania, claim TL:ROU:event:1918:union-of-transylvania-with-romania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Greater Romania
claims.summary: With Bessarabia, Bukovina and Transylvania joined to the kingdom, Romania nearly doubled in size, gaining large Hungarian and German minorities within its enlarged borders.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1918-greater-romania, claim TL:ROU:event:1918:greater-romania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Trianon
claims.summary: The Treaty of Trianon formally transferred Transylvania and part of the Banat from Hungary to Romania, stripping Hungary of about two-thirds of its territory and leaving a lasting dispute.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1920-treaty-of-trianon, claim TL:ROU:event:1920:treaty-of-trianon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Soviet seizure of Bessarabia and northern Bukovina
claims.summary: The Soviet Union demanded and took Bessarabia and northern Bukovina from Romania, the first of the 1940 territorial losses; Bessarabia, largely Romanian-speaking, became the core of the later Republic of Moldova.

sources.label: Moldova and Romania: A Long and Complicated Relationship

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1940-soviet-seizure-of-bessarabia-and-northern, claim TL:ROU:event:1940:soviet-seizure-of-bessarabia-and-northern, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Vienna Award and Southern Dobruja
claims.summary: Under German and Italian arbitration Romania ceded northern Transylvania to Hungary; in September southern Dobruja was ceded to Bulgaria, costing Romania about 30% of its territory and people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1940-second-vienna-award-and-southern-dobruja, claim TL:ROU:event:1940:second-vienna-award-and-southern-dobruja, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Romania joins the Axis
claims.summary: After the loss of King Carol II's throne, General Ion Antonescu took power and brought Romania into the Axis, later joining the war against the Soviet Union and presiding over the murder of hundreds of thousands of Jews and Roma.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1940-romania-joins-the-axis, claim TL:ROU:event:1940:romania-joins-the-axis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Communist takeover and the People's Republic
claims.summary: After the war Romania was drawn into the Soviet bloc; the Paris treaty restored northern Transylvania, but Bessarabia stayed Soviet, the monarchy was abolished and a communist People's Republic proclaimed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1947-communist-takeover-and-the-people-s-republic, claim TL:ROU:event:1947:communist-takeover-and-the-people-s-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ceausescu dictatorship
claims.summary: Nicolae Ceausescu ruled Romania from 1965, pursuing a foreign policy independent of Moscow while imposing a personality cult, pervasive secret-police control and harsh 1980s austerity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1965-the-ceausescu-dictatorship, claim TL:ROU:event:1965:the-ceausescu-dictatorship, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Romanian Revolution
claims.summary: Protests beginning in Timisoara spread to Bucharest; the army turned against the regime, the Ceausescus fled on 22 December and were executed on 25 December 1989, ending communist rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1989-the-romanian-revolution, claim TL:ROU:event:1989:the-romanian-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Romania joins NATO
claims.summary: Romania formally joined NATO on 29 March 2004, depositing its instrument of accession in Washington alongside six other new members in the alliance's largest round of enlargement.

sources.label: Seven new members join NATO, 29 March 2004

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-2004-romania-joins-nato, claim TL:ROU:event:2004:romania-joins-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: On 1 January 2007 Romania, with Bulgaria, joined the European Union, raising it to twenty-seven member states and completing Romania's integration into the West.

sources.label: Bulgaria and Romania join the European Union

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-2007-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:ROU:event:2007:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Moldova's independence and the Romanian bond
claims.summary: As the Soviet Union dissolved, the former Bessarabia declared independence as the Republic of Moldova, immediately recognised by Romania, with which it shares the Romanian language and a common history.

sources.label: Moldova and Romania: A Long and Complicated Relationship

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-1991-moldova-s-independence-and-the-romanian-bond, claim TL:ROU:event:1991:moldova-s-independence-and-the-romanian-bond, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ICJ Black Sea boundary with Ukraine
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice fixed the Romania–Ukraine maritime boundary in the Black Sea, ruling that Ukraine's Serpents' Island would have no effect beyond its 12-mile territorial sea.

sources.label: Maritime Delimitation in the Black Sea (Romania v. Ukraine), Judgment of 3 February 2009

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Romania: From Roman Dacia to the European Union — a Latin island in a Slavic and Magyar sea, unified, dismembered and remade.", terralore.co/country/ROU/chronicle#ev-2009-icj-black-sea-boundary-with-ukraine, claim TL:ROU:event:2009:icj-black-sea-boundary-with-ukraine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
